title: Simple Silky Lemon Cream Posset
summary: The simplest posset: cream and sugar boiled together and set with fresh lemon juice into a silky, tangy cream.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Reduce
steps.text: bring the cream, sugar and salt to the boil in the pan, stirring, then boil steadily 6-8 min, stirring often, until reduced to about 480 ml. Lift off the heat if it rises. Reducing concentrates the cream so it sets firmly.

steps.title: Sharpen
steps.text: off the heat, stir in the lemon juice; it will thicken a little at once. Acid makes the milk proteins thicken the cream.

steps.title: Settle
steps.text: leave 15-20 min until a skin begins to form, then stir and pour into the jug.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: divide between the glasses and chill uncovered for 3 h, until set like a soft cream. Cover after that. Leaving it uncovered stops drips from condensation.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: take out of the fridge 10 min before eating so it is silky, not stiff.

tips: A common mistake is not boiling long enough, so the posset stays runny; boil it for the full time.
Use freshly squeezed lemon juice, not bottled.
Serve with crisp biscuits for crunch.
storage: Cover once set and keep in the fridge for up to 2 days. Do not freeze.
